title: Varonis documents TheMailer, a self-hosted phishing kit that uses commercial AI models to reach inboxes
date_note: Publication date not stated on the Varonis page; coverage appeared November 17-18.
summary: Varonis Threat Labs describes TheMailer, a self-hosted phishing platform sold for a lifetime licence of about $3,000 to $6,000. It uses operator-supplied keys for AI services to rewrite lures, send test emails and retry until they reach the inbox. A sample target list held 145,133 mostly Japanese .co.jp and .ac.jp addresses.
plain: A phishing kit sold to criminals uses AI chatbots to rewrite scam emails until spam filters let them through.
exec: Per-recipient rewriting defeats content-based email filtering, so defences must rely on sender behaviour and link checks.
action: Enforce SPF, DKIM and DMARC at p=reject, check links through the full redirect chain at click time, and tune detection to sender behaviour rather than message content.

validation.note: Varonis' own write-up read in full; Dark Reading carries it but its page refused automated reading. Vendor also promotes its own product.

review.note: Varonis post: 3,000-6,000 USD licence, operator API keys, 145,133 mostly .co.jp/.ac.jp entries match; publication date not visible on page.
